acm_short_paper_assessment.reason: Official ACM article-type documentation defines Short Paper as an APC-eligible, fully peer-reviewed article that reports on original research, contains many of the same characteristics as a Research Article, and is intended to be self-contained—distinct from Non-APC-Eligible types such as Demonstration, Extended abstract, Poster, and Work in Progress. Protocol Amendment 003 specifies that report completeness is judged by substantive primary-research content (method/architecture, system/assumptions, evaluation method, and analyzable results) rather than page count or a venue label such as 'short paper'. Keeping the database-level instruction 'Do not include Short-Paper' would therefore risk excluding substantively complete primary-research reports before full-text screening.
